Montjuïc is more than an emblematic mountain within the urban fabric of Barcelona; it is the summit that has witnessed its historical evolution. In this context, this intervention is located between two significant mountain climbs.

The appearance of the ‘mountain refuge’ is proposed, activating a space that favors contemplation and encounter, in a place full of history, such as Casaramona or the pavilion of Mies, and monumentalitybut with a look at the neighborhood and its people. 6e5328e348db15724c39f07f11be19bd847eb7bb:
*Matosinhos, Porto*
Taller Belén Ramos
Three houses-workshops for artists
/
The sculptor eagerly recognized the house that Souto de Moura had had built decades ago. When he came across the farm where he would spend the next few summers, everything seemed scattered, as if they had been putting together pieces of walls, roofs, empty spaces and orchards, picking them up one by one, like someone who mounts a wall with found stones. But little by little, with each alignment, with each new wall raised, a compass of volumes was discoveredmodulated, recognizing the dynamic character of the alleys, roofs and boats of Matosinhos. The concrete walls seen, almost like centuries-old statues, showed the scars that the rainwater had been leaving, while the upper part deformed to become an open channel, distributing the stream of zinc roofs towards the orchards and the border forest. He was surprised to be greeted by an outdoor space that, withoutfunnels, he showed the door of the workshop where he would create his new collection. Through a gap, a distributor courtyard opened up, a modern cloister, which gave access to the rest rooms of the estate. As if he had never left the alleys of Matosinhos, he was now discovering a small town that, without realizing it, would become his home.

Arrived at a well-lit room, he settled in, before moving on to the living roomof being. In that courtyard protected by walls, I could already see summer lunches with company. A discreet kitchen accompanied the space with a counter that crossed the load-bearing wall, communicating with the outside courtyard. The sculptor went to the last room. The workshop was spacious and laid out between two concrete walls. He appreciated the texture of the formwork once inside.

This border was crossed by a large sliding door, made ofsheet metal and memories of the industrial port, which he had to push hard. Once the threshold was crossed, a small era unfolded, flanked by the old orchards that were traced between the two walls. As he contemplated that scenario, he was struck by the cry of his new neighbor, a writer immersed in his novel, who also seemed captivated by the place. He insisted on recording the first impressions that this architecture had aroused in- Him.

*Vestuari a la platja de la Barceloneta*
Taller Carme Ribas & Miquel Mariner, $el tercer temps$
/
The project invites you to find a hidden shell in the plenum. An artifice . The void that a body generates when it wrinkles is filled with a paste that dries with a clear gravitational impact. These pieces, as soon as they are strategically grouped, will become the hollow of a shell, a wrapper that wraps them up. Two incisions cut out this thin film, which gives a glimpse of an entrance and exit filter in what will be a new costume for the beach.A ritual of what is naked, dressed, and finally completely undressed. The change of scale allows a generating body to close a space where human bodies hide, breathe, wipe, enter and exit. The unit of measurement remains what lies between two hands or two feet.

*Es Molinar, Palma de Mallorca*
Taller Arnau Sastre, $hcc etsab$
/
A repetition of overlaps crosses the entire plot and becomes a white canvas that the project takes as a starting point. On this support, the space is not filled homogeneously, but is stressed in gravities: elements that attract uses and looks.

These devices appear in contact with the built border of the interior of the island, increasing the potential of the old stone courtyards, and also within the new interiors,exploring new ways to schedule and unschedule such stays. The ground floor courtyards act as filters of ventilation and intimacy, while the modules that open towards the interior of the island transform this level into a space for meeting, exhibition and coexistence, where daily life is amplified as a collective event.
6247529ba893cb02a242cd3f36bdd3c6c61c0b82:
*Boavista, Porto*
Taller Belén Ramos
/
Conjunt d'oficines-taller a Porto. 
Antigament, un conjunt fabril era protagonista d’un terreny entre camps i alguns petits nuclis urbans. Durant dècades, aquesta zona ha estat edificada gradualment amb usos variats, ocupant espais verds que la pluja havia regat, i amagant rierols que abans eren part de la sonoritat del paisatge urbà.

La topografia configura el lloc com un aqüífer obert natural. El conjunt se situa de manera que queda protegit de possibles inundacions; el nou canal és alhora camí i barrera. L’aigua recollida pel sistema de cobertes es canalitza per baixants fins a retornar al canal. D’aquesta manera, es tanca el cicle de l’aigua i es minimitza la petjada de la nova construcció.
d99bdd3aa1b6288775192678b998ede62c364c5c:
*Es Molinar, Palma de Mallorca*
Taller Arnau Sastre, $hcc etsab$
/
Una repetició d’encavallades travessa tota la parcel·la i esdevé un llenç blanc que el projecte assumeix com a punt de partida. Sobre aquest suport, l’espai no s’omple de manera homogènia, sinó que es tensiona en gravetats: elements que atrauen usos i mirades. 

Aquests dispositius apareixen en contacte amb la frontera construïda de l’interior d’illa, augmentant les potencialitats dels vells patis de pedra, i també dins dels nous habitacles, explorant noves maneres de programar i desprogramar tals estances. Els patis de planta baixa actuen com filtres de ventilació i intimitat, mentre que els mòduls que s’obren cap a l’interior d’illa transformen aquest nivell en un espai de trobada, exposició i convivència, on la vida quotidiana s’amplifica com a fet col·lectiu.

Pau is 24 years old, the middle brother, and works as a communicator and designer at an alternative company. He loves his job, but even more than that he loves coming home at the end of the day and watching the afternoon light stream in through the window, reminding him of Menorca. He has a soft spot for summer, long afternoons, and Mediterranean architecture.

However, what really drives him is dance. He's been dancing since he was little, and for him it's both a refuge and a way to connect with space. When he dances, everything falls into place: the body, the air, the silence. It's another way of communicating, more sincere than any word.

Pau is six feet tall, but he doesn't define himself by it. He's only grateful for it when he can move freely, without bumping into ceilings or tripping over chairs. In the end, it all comes down to this: finding spaces where he can be himself.

A repetition of steel trusses traverses all of plot and becomes a blank canvas that the project takes as its starting point. On this support, the space is not filled homogeneously but is instead tensioned by gravities: elements that attract uses and gazes. 

These devices appear in contact with the built boundary of the inner block, enhancing the potential of the old stone courtyardss, and also within the new dwellingss, exploring new ways to program and unprogram such spaces. The courtyardss of the lower floor plan act as filters for ventilation and privacy, while the moduless that open onto the courtyard transform this level into a space for gathering, exhibition, and socializing, where everyday life is amplified as a collective experience.

En Pau té 24 anys, és el germà del mig i treballa com a comunicador i dissenyador en una empresa alternativa. Li encanta la seva feina, però encara més arribar a casa al final del dia i mirar com la llum de la tarda entra per la finestra, recordant-li Menorca. Té debilitat per l’estiu, les tardes llargues i l’arquitectura mediterrània.
However, what really drives him is dance. He has been dancing since he was a child, and for him it is as much a refuge as a way to connect with space. When he dances, everything falls into place: the body, the air, the silence. It is another way of communicating, more sincere than any word.

Pau is six feet tall, but he doesn't define himself by it. He's only grateful for it when he can move freely, without bumping into ceilings or tripping over chairs. In the end, it all comes down to this: finding spaces where he can be himself.

Office complex workshop in Porto. 
 Formerly, a factory complex was the centerpiece of a terrain between fields and some small urban settlements. For decades, this area has been gradually built up with varied uses, occupying green spaces that rain had watered and hiding streams that were once part of the urban landscape's soundscape. 

The topography shapes the site like a natural open aquifer. The complex is positioned to be protected from potential flooding; the new channel serves both as a pathway and a barrier. Water collected by the roofs system is channeled through downspouts back to the channel. In this way, the water cycle is closed and the new construction's footprint is minimized.
